quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride. The horn button is usually found next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Increase your ability to be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of other drivers' blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, protects your lane, signals your intentions, avoids wind from other vehicles, and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: If you are not traveling slowly enough when shifting into a lower gear, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you are going too fast when you shift to a lower gear, the motorcycle will lurch forward and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly and keep going straight. Ease off the throttle. Apply the brake to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Which of the following types of footwear is best for a motorcycle operator?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high-top shoes that support your ankles. Laced-up boots are best. If your boots have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: To accommodate a passenger, you may have to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust the shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, so you may need to adjust the motorcycle's shocks. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while taking a curve is often the result of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast for the conditions can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Of the following, which clothing item will not reduce injuries in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: Common drugs, such as cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect a rider's abilities to safely operate their motorcycle.
Usually won't affect a rider's abilities to safely operate their motorcycle.
Pose no risk to a rider's operating abilities.
Are always acceptable to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect a rider's abilities to safely operate their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Know the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: When braking:

options.text: Use only one brake if it is a non-emergency situation.
Only use both brakes if you are riding on wet pavement.
Use both brakes regardless of the circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes regardless of the circumstances.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Turns corners the same way as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Turns corners differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used on curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turns corners differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar does not turn corners the same way as a regular two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make riding more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter medications, prescription medications, and illegal drugs, have side effects that can make it unsafe to ride.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is safer than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing over time, even when wearing a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. Use your left foot to shift. Lift your foot under the lever to shift up. Press down to shift down.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Ride slowly toward the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slowly toward the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it. Then speed up and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: A helmet will not provide the best protection:

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it is free of defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has cracks.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT standards, fit snugly, and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or broken straps.

questions.question: Which is NOT protective clothing for riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Keep the fuel valve open.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. You will more likely notice a change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: Increase your following distance:

options.text: If there are only a few vehicles on the roadway.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the roadway is slippery.
questions.explanation: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: If your motorcycle handles differently while riding, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in handling may mean a tire has failed. If your motorcycle feels different, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should apply throttle and:

options.text: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Apply throttle through a turn to stabilize your suspension. Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly through the turn.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can slow down by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting.
questions.explanation: Riders often slow down by downshifting. Know that downshifting does not turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: Checking your motorcycle before riding:

options.text: Is only useful if a mechanic does it.
Should not be done before riding.
Should only be done after riding.
Can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know they see you.
Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not notice them.

questions.question: If you must brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than on a straight road.
Brake as hard as on a straight road.
Wait until you exit the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when your motorcycle is leaning. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, brake gently and smoothly.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers all provide poor grip for motorcycle tires. Dry pavement provides the best grip.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Only use mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between motorcyclists and other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where conflicts between motorcyclists and other drivers happen most often. Be extra careful when entering and riding through intersections.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane has oil on it and is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: What do experienced riders do?

options.text: Change positions within their lane as conditions change.
Stay in one part of the lane at all times.
Weave within the lane to be more visible.
Travel only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change positions within their lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders have three position choices in their lane. Pick the safest position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, all riders should stop.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?

options.text: Up to a judge to decide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Severe.
questions.explanation: Oregon law has severe mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Riders should check their mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders who are new to their motorcycles.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Focus on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look at motorcycles without noticing them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and appear to be moving more slowly than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their actual distance and speed.

questions.question: Motorists entering a highway from an entrance ramp to your right may not see you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left part of your lane so they can share it, if needed.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles merging from an entrance ramp. Change lanes away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to enter safely.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have rounded, or convex, mirrors. These mirrors:

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars look closer than they really are.
Show only a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they actually are. If you are not used to them, practice judging distances in convex mirrors.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden on a motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has ridden on a motorcycle before and explain what to do.
Not explain anything since they are only a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has ridden on a motorcycle before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to ride safely. Never assume they already know what to do. Give complete instructions before every ride.

questions.question: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, it is usually safest to:

options.text: Ride straight ahead within your lane to cross the tracks.
Turn to cross the tracks at a sharp angle.
Cross by riding on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight ahead within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks by riding straight ahead in your lane. Turning to cross at a sharp angle is dangerous because you could enter another lane.

questions.question: To protect yourself while riding, your pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose your legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. They should fit snugly enough to not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they restrict movement.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: You can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Leave more space if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Increase following distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: One way to tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding is if:

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: A flat rear tire will cause the back of your motorcycle to jerk side to side. You may not hear a tire fail while riding.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another driver on the left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane to be seen in their side mirror.
Move to the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of your lane to be seen in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left side of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to see ahead better and be more visible. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Protects your whole face, not just your eyes.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator discourage other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers.
By riding in the center of the lane.
By riding in the left part of the lane.
By riding in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to leave no large spaces on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.
